query:
The Harrington family operates with a norm that Sunday evening is family chat time — everyone checks in at least once over the weekend. Based on the conversations, does this hold equally for all family members — or does someone consistently relate to it differently, and what tells you that?

Options:
A. Marcus
B. Luis
C. Rob
D. Jess
context:
[1] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2026-02-10T19:23:00) To be fair the grandchildren visit argument is actually one of the stronger predictors of whether extended family stays close across generations. I'm supportive. Also I want to flag something separately -- Dad, how's the knee been this week? You seemed to be favouring it on Saturday when Bev was over.
[2] (about=Luis, episodic, t6 @2026-01-27T20:15:00) Marcus running a Harrington game night via calendar invite is somehow the most satisfying development of 2026 so far. I'm in, even if I have to video-in too. This is what family should feel like! Also Jess wants me to tell everyone her thighs are still sore 😂
[3] (about=Marcus, episodic, t6 @2026-01-27T20:04:00) Tyler I promise you will leave understanding it. I've run this teach three times now. I actually enjoy the setup more than most people enjoy playing, to be honest. The rules are half the fun. Dad, are you and Mom interested? I can do a Saturday afternoon so it's not a late night.
[4] (about=Rob, episodic, t6 @2026-01-27T20:09:00) Can't make it if it's before February 12, Priya has her 20-week scan on the 10th and we're staying close to home that week. After that we're free most Saturdays. What are you thinking, Marcus?
[5] (about=Luis, episodic, t0 @2026-01-06T19:40:00) HAPPY NEW YEAR Harringtons!! We're doing good out here, the kids are already complaining about going back to school which honestly same 😂 Dennis I respect the stubbornness but a bad knee is like a bad mise en place, you CANNOT just power through it and expect good results. Trust the process!
[6] (about=Marcus, episodic, t13 @2026-02-24T19:15:00) Game night report: Saturday went well. Tyler beat everyone at Wingspan despite claiming not to understand the engine-building mechanic, which I refuse to accept was genuine. Mom and Dad stayed until 6pm which is a record. Dana brought the wine and left before cleanup, which is also a record but in a different direction. To be fair, everyone seemed to actually enjoy it.
[7] (about=Luis, episodic, t10 @2026-02-10T19:15:00) Carol okay I have to be honest, that hit me harder than I expected. My mom said something similar last month. I've been thinking -- one Columbus trip a year isn't enough anymore. The kids are at the age where they need the grandparents in the room, not just on a screen. I want to talk about doing a second trip this year. Summer is obvious but what about fall too? I can work around the restaurant schedule.
[8] (about=Jess, episodic, t10 @2026-02-10T19:17:00) Luis has been saying this for a year actually and I kept saying flights are expensive but I think he's right. The kids were shy with Dad on that tablet call at first. That was a flag. Let me look at October, we might be able to do a long weekend around Columbus Day.
[9] (about=Carol, episodic, t8 @2026-02-03T19:19:00) So while I was at class, Jess your Mia video called Dad on the tablet!! She wanted to show him the drawing she made of the garden and he actually stayed on the call for twenty minutes!! He called me after and said 'that tablet is actually useful.' Dennis Harrington said that. About technology!! 😱😱
[10] (about=Dennis, episodic, t6 @2026-01-27T20:06:00) Depends on the Saturday.
agent_answer:
**B. Luis**

Luis is the one who consistently relates to the family’s weekend check-in norm differently: he does **not** treat a screen-based check-in as enough. He says the kids “need the grandparents in the room, not just on a screen” and wants a second in-person trip, because “one Columbus trip a year isn’t enough anymore” (excerpt [7]).

Jess even confirms this has been a consistent position, not a one-off: “Luis has been saying this for a year actually” (excerpt [8]). So while the others engage with the usual weekend/check-in rhythm — Marcus organizing Saturday game nights, Rob responding with availability and offers to drive over, Jess eventually agreeing — Luis is the one pushing for something beyond the Sunday-evening chat/tablet call.

query:
The Harrington family has an expectation that big news — jobs, health, relationships — gets announced in the family chat before spreading to extended family. Based on what the conversations show, does everyone follow this norm — or does one member appear to have a different relationship to it, and what tells you that?

Options:
A. Dana
B. Carol
C. Tyler
D. Priya
context:
[1] (about=Rob, episodic, t2 @2026-01-13T19:17:00) Mom, Priya literally just said quiet visit. Two minutes ago. In this chat.
[2] (about=Priya, episodic, t2 @2026-01-13T19:11:00) Ha Carol we are definitely finding out. Name list is very much in progress. :) And yes we should come to Columbus soon, though I'd honestly just love a quiet visit (though of course your call on what to plan). No pressure on a big gathering right now.
[3] (about=Bev, episodic, t2 @2026-01-13T19:15:00) Rob, Priya, wonderful news. Love you both. Carol, Priya said quiet visit. Love you too.
[4] (about=Carol, episodic, t2 @2026-01-13T19:13:00) Oh we'll keep it simple!! Just the family!! Maybe Bev, and Marcus and Dana are right here, and I'll invite Aunt Sheila from Dayton because she'll be so thrilled!! 😊 just a little gathering!! just let me know when!!
[5] (about=Carol, episodic, t2 @2026-01-13T19:09:00) Tyler you are already family!! 💛 I need to know everything, Priya, do you have a name list yet, are you finding out the gender, when are you coming to Columbus so I can cook for you!! just let me know and I'll plan everything!! 🙌🙌
[6] (about=Rob, episodic, t12 @2026-02-17T19:29:00) I want to say something here. I've always been against extended family stays, you all know that, too many people in the house for too long is not my thing. But the last few weeks with Priya having a rough time and it just being the two of us has made me think differently. I think we should talk about being closer to family before the baby arrives. Not moving, but more actual time. Longer visits, both directions. R
[7] (about=Priya, episodic, t12 @2026-02-17T19:26:00) Really glad to hear that about Dennis. On a different note -- I want to mention something. The past few weeks have been harder than I let on earlier (though of course nothing alarming, just more fatigue and some nausea that came back which apparently is normal). Rob has been great but I've been thinking a lot about how far Cleveland is from everyone.
[8] (about=Luis, episodic, t14 @2026-02-24T19:35:00) Priya that is the best thing I've read in this chat since the pregnancy announcement and that was pretty good. Also just want to say -- watching Rob, Dana, and Marcus all run interference on Carol's guest list in real time is genuinely beautiful sibling choreography. You three have finally become a unit. 😂
[9] (about=Carol, episodic, t14 @2026-02-24T19:37:00) I am NOT being managed 🙄 I am simply enthusiastic!! But fine, just Rob and Priya Saturday, Bev on Sunday, and then we'll all have a proper dinner another time!! I'm still making the soup!! 🍲
[10] (about=Bev, episodic, t14 @2026-02-24T19:49:00) There it is. Love you all. Carol, great bones on this family right now. Priced to move in the right direction.
agent_answer:
B. Carol.

Carol is the one who has a different relationship to the norm. When Priya announces the pregnancy and explicitly says she'd love a "quiet visit" and "no pressure on a big gathering right now," Carol immediately starts planning to spread the news outward and expand the circle: "I'll invite Aunt Sheila from Dayton because she'll be so thrilled!! 😊 just a little gathering!!" — Aunt Sheila being extended family. Carol also pushes for details ("do you have a name list yet, are you finding out the gender... I'll plan everything!!") and keeps trying to add people, until Rob, Dana, and Marcus have to "run interference on Carol's guest list" (per Luis) to keep it small.

The others — Priya and Rob (the news-sharers themselves), Tyler (celebrating in-chat), Dana, and Marcus — don't show any sign of spreading the news beyond the family chat; Carol is the one repeatedly trying to broadcast it to the extended family against Priya's stated wish for quiet.
